entries.grounds: The version/commit-mismatch branch (review_ocr.py:271-273) loses ': declares itself ', so the reason becomes `{exe}{seen.version} ({seen.commit}), not the pinned {OCR.version} ({OCR.commit[:7]}): no review command was run` — for 'another version': `/x/ocrv1.11.0 (182898c), not the pinned v1.12.12 (182898c): no review command was run`. The exe glues onto the declared version and the self-declaration verb is gone. Decisively, the branch then contains NO DECLARED_WAYS marker ('declares itself','exited','did not answer in time','printed no version line','could not be started' are all absent), so run.ocr_identity's reader `(marker,) = [m for m in DECLARED_WAYS if m in reason]` (test_v21_ocr_identity.py:197) unpacks an empty list and raises ValueError — that test FAILS on this mutant (reasoned from code; not run, per the hard rule limiting runs to the two registered kill files). RAN registered kill files: ocr_declared+ocr_gate PASS (22 OK, 77.7s) because both assert VALUE words + '/x/ocr' only (the glued '/x/ocrv1.11.0' still contains '/x/ocr'); the positional kill files do not pin the self-declaration.
entries.refutation: A reader depends on 'declares itself'. Reader: run.ocr_identity's reason, consumed at test_v21_ocr_identity.py:186-202 `(marker,) = [m for m in DECLARED_WAYS if m in reason]` (ValueError when no marker is present), and the operator reading the journaled 'reviewer cannot run: ...' / run.ocr_refusal text, who relies on the verb framing the pair as the binary's self-declaration — the entire contract of this branch (docstring review_ocr.py:256 'This is a SELF-DECLARATION'). Input: `review_ocr.declared('/x/ocr', 0, 'open-code-review v1.11.0 (182898c) darwin/arm64\n')` (any version/commit mismatch; exit 0). Owed in the positional kill file tests/v2/test_v21_ocr_declared.py — in test_every_answer_that_is_not_the_pinned_build... (:72-80) or test_a_mismatch_names_both... (:82-85): add `self.assertIn('declares itself', why)` for the mismatch answers. Note: the behaviour is already caught incidentally by test_v21_ocr_identity.py:186-202 (not a registered kill file for this target), so the gap is POSITIONAL (the self-declaration is unpinned in declared()'s own kill files), not an unprotected behaviour.
